raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`Req.update_finish_state` applies a pending abort before it checks the step's own stop token, stop string and length cap. When the step that commits a client abort (`/abort_request`) also reached EOS or `max_new_tokens`, the request finishes as an abort with every committed token. With speculative decoding one step commits several tokens, so the output can carry tokens after the EOS or past `max_new_tokens`. Clients that abort requests and keep the partial outputs then receive tokens past a stop.

Related: open #44874 caps aborted speculative output at `max_new_tokens` and keeps the abort reason. This PR covers stop tokens and stop strings too, and reports the step's own finish (`stop` / `length`) for client aborts only; aborts that carry a status code (intake rejections, timeouts, the 499 case in #44874) keep their reason, so the two do not conflict in behavior.

## Modifications

- `Req.update_finish_state`: a client abort (`FINISH_ABORT` with no status code) yields to the stop token, stop string or length cap reached in the same step, which then trims the output as usual. Aborts with a status code keep their reason.
- Visible to clients: a request aborted with `/abort_request` (or by a session abort) in the step where it reaches a stop token, a stop string or `max_new_tokens` now returns `finish_reason` `stop` or `length` instead of `abort`, with the output trimmed at the stop or the cap.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_finish_length_speculative.py` (CPU), 5 new cases: EOS, stop string and length cap in the abort step win and trim; an abort without a step finish stays an abort; an abort with a status code keeps its reason. The first 3 fail on main.

## Accuracy Tests

Requests that are not aborted run the same code. Driving the real `Req.update_finish_state` on CPU, with a client abort pending:

| step commits | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `[10, 11, EOS, 20]` (EOS mid-run) | abort, 4 tokens incl. one after EOS | `stop`, `[10, 11, EOS]` |
| `[10, STOP, 20]`, stop string "STOP" | abort, 3 tokens | `stop`, `[10, STOP]` |
| run crossing `max_new_tokens=4` | abort, 5 tokens | `length`, 4 tokens |
| no stop, no cap | abort | abort (unchanged) |
| abort with status 503 + EOS | abort | abort (unchanged) |

End to end, the race (abort arriving in exactly the finishing step) is timing-dependent and was not reproduced on GPU.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed impact: the finish checks run once more only in the step that applies a client abort.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No documented field changes; the finish reason of such a client abort is now `stop` or `length` (see Modifications), matching the output it returns.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Unit-level evidence above; no GPU repro of the race, no speed change.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).


Prepared with the help of Claude Code; every result above was measured as described.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`

@@ -1436,8 +1436,19 @@ def update_finish_state(self, new_accepted_len: int = 1):
             return
 
         if self.to_finish:
-            self.finished_reason = self.to_finish
-            self.to_finish = None
+            to_finish, self.to_finish = self.to_finish, None
+            # A client abort (no status code) that lands in the step reaching a
+            # stop token, stop string or max_new_tokens yields to that finish,
+            # so the output never runs past it.
+            if (
+                new_accepted_len > 0
+                and isinstance(to_finish, FINISH_ABORT)
+                and to_finish.status_code is None
+            ):
+                self.update_finish_state(new_accepted_len)
+                if self.finished():
+                    return
+            self.finished_reason = to_finish
             return
 
         new_accepted_tokens = self.output_ids[-new_accepted_len:]

@@ -19,6 +19,7 @@
 maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
 
 from sglang.srt.managers.req_types import (
+    FINISH_ABORT,
     FINISH_LENGTH,
     FINISH_MATCHED_STR,
     FINISH_MATCHED_TOKEN,
@@ -76,6 +77,50 @@ def _make_req(
     return req
 
 
+class TestClientAbortYieldsToStepFinish(CustomTestCase):
+    """A client abort (no status code) applied at the commit of a step that
+    reaches a stop or the length cap reports that finish and trims at it."""
+
+    def _abort_step(self, output_ids, accepted, abort, **kwargs):
+        req = _make_req(output_ids, **kwargs)
+        req.request_finish(abort)
+        req.update_finish_state(new_accepted_len=accepted)
+        self.assertIsNone(req.to_finish)
+        return req
+
+    def test_eos_in_the_abort_step_wins(self):
+        req = self._abort_step(
+            [10, 11, EOS_ID, 20], 3, FINISH_ABORT(), max_new_tokens=16
+        )
+        self.assertIsInstance(req.finished_reason, FINISH_MATCHED_TOKEN)
+        self.assertEqual(list(req.output_ids_through_stop), [10, 11, EOS_ID])
+
+    def test_stop_str_in_the_abort_step_wins(self):
+        req = self._abort_step(
+            [10, STOP_ID, 20], 2, FINISH_ABORT(), max_new_tokens=16, stop=["STOP"]
+        )
+        self.assertIsInstance(req.finished_reason, FINISH_MATCHED_STR)
+        self.assertEqual(list(req.output_ids_through_stop), [10, STOP_ID])
+
+    def test_length_cap_in_the_abort_step_wins(self):
+        req = self._abort_step(
+            [10, 11, 12, 20, 21], 3, FINISH_ABORT(), max_new_tokens=4
+        )
+        self.assertIsInstance(req.finished_reason, FINISH_LENGTH)
+        self.assertEqual(list(req.output_ids_through_stop), [10, 11, 12, 20])
+
+    def test_abort_without_a_step_finish_stays_an_abort(self):
+        abort = FINISH_ABORT()
+        req = self._abort_step([10, 11, 12], 2, abort, max_new_tokens=16)
+        self.assertIs(req.finished_reason, abort)
+        self.assertEqual(list(req.output_ids_through_stop), [10, 11, 12])
+
+    def test_abort_with_a_status_code_keeps_its_reason(self):
+        abort = FINISH_ABORT("timed out", 503)
+        req = self._abort_step([10, EOS_ID], 2, abort, max_new_tokens=16)
+        self.assertIs(req.finished_reason, abort)
+
+
